390.indexes:
SPY and QQQ are at their highs: QQQ closed over its two-week line on 2 Oct 2026 and sits +1.0% above it (resistance turned support, RSI 68); SPY closed −0.6% from its line and is +0.0% from it live.

IWM and RSP are not there. Both sit under their 21-, 50- and 100-day averages and over a rising 200-day, −7.1% and −5.2% from their August highs, with RSI 44 and 43 and Geigers in the lowest 13% of their own year. The rebound so far is +2.0% and +1.5% off the low and +1.2% and +0.7% over five sessions: a bounce inside a pullback, not yet a turn (neither has its 21-day back).

Read together: the two cap-weighted indexes say uptrend at resistance; the two that count every stock say an uptrend that has pulled back to where leaders-on-a-pullback are bought. That is the same split REGIME shows as "breadth not joining".
390.midpoint:
Today is that case: heat +0.08 (middling) with leadership narrow (the heat's own concentration and equal-weight readings average −0.88). In two years it happened on 34 sessions in 10 separate stretches; the current stretch is the longest.

What followed, counted. Over the next 60 sessions SPY beat the equal-weight S&P on 0 of 21 of those sessions and beat our median company on 7 of 21; over the next 20, on 3 and 4 of 21. On middling days with broad leadership it was the other way round: SPY beat equal-weight on 116 of 155.

So: the July ladder has no index sleeve at all — at 50% it spreads the money across sectors by their readings — so "more index" is not its natural answer; it is something we would add. And the count does not back adding the cap-weighted index at this point: after narrow, middling stretches the average stock caught up every time it could be measured. If the midpoint calls for an index, the count points to the equal-weight one (RSP) or simply to the names that are cold for themselves. It is 21 sessions in three clusters (Dec 2024, Nov 2025, Apr–May 2026): a hint, not a rule.
